items.stem: A pipeline step is retried after a transient failure and sometimes inserts duplicate rows. Which property should the step have to make retries safe?

options.rationale: Correct: an idempotent step produces the same result whether run once or many times, so retries do not duplicate data.
More parallelism does not prevent duplicate inserts on retry.
Batch size does not control duplication on re-run.
Switching to streaming does not by itself make a step idempotent.

items.explanation: Correct: an idempotent step produces the same result whether run once or many times, so retries do not duplicate data.

items.stem: Which extraction approach pulls only rows changed since the last run using a tracked boundary value?

options.text: Incremental extraction with a high-water mark
options.rationale: Correct: a high-water mark records the last processed boundary so only newer rows are pulled.
Full extraction reloads everything and does not use a boundary.
Sampling pulls a subset, not specifically changed rows.
Schema-on-read concerns interpretation at query time, not which rows are extracted.

items.explanation: Correct: a high-water mark records the last processed boundary so only newer rows are pulled.

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the reliability of a data pipeline? (Select TWO)

options.text: Routing invalid records to a dead-letter path for review
options.rationale: Correct: isolating bad records keeps the batch running and preserves them for investigation.

options.text: Making load steps idempotent so re-runs are safe
options.rationale: Correct: idempotent loads make retries and reprocessing safe.

options.text: Silently dropping any row that fails validation
options.rationale: Silent drops hide data loss and make failures hard to detect.

options.text: Disabling all retries to avoid duplicates
options.rationale: The fix for retry duplication is idempotency, not removing resilience.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating bad records keeps the batch running and preserves them for investigation.
